import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History: JOIN on ["name", "school"]
# Source0 columns: ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
# Source1 columns: ['Student ID', 'name', 'gender', 'grade', 'school', 'reading_score', 'math_score']
# Join keys: Source0.name == Source1.school

# Rename Source0 'name' to 'school' to match Source1 'school' for join
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={"name": "school"})

# Perform inner join on 'school'
joined = pd.merge(df0_renamed, df1, on="school", how="inner")

# Now transform to target schema:
# Target Schema: 
# ['School Name': string, 'Student Grade': string, 'School ID': integer, 'School Size': integer, 
#  'School Budget': integer, 'Student ID': float, 'Student Reading Score': float, 'Average Student Math Score': float]

# Map columns accordingly:
# 'School Name' <- 'school' (string)
# 'Student Grade' <- 'grade' (string)
# 'School ID' <- 'School ID' (int)
# 'School Size' <- 'size' (int)
# 'School Budget' <- 'budget' (int)
# 'Student ID' <- 'Student ID' (float)
# 'Student Reading Score' <- 'reading_score' (float)
# 'Average Student Math Score' <- 'math_score' (float)

# Convert types explicitly to match target schema
result = pd.DataFrame({
    "School Name": joined["school"].astype(str),
    "Student Grade": joined["grade"].astype(str),
    "School ID": joined["School ID"].astype(int),
    "School Size": joined["size"].astype(int),
    "School Budget": joined["budget"].astype(int),
    "Student ID": joined["Student ID"].astype(float),
    "Student Reading Score": joined["reading_score"].astype(float),
    "Average Student Math Score": joined["math_score"].astype(float),
})

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Rename columns in source1 to match target schema where applicable
# We'll rename 'school' to 'name' to join on school name
# But since source0 has 'name' as school name, join on source0.name = source1.school
# After join, rename columns to target schema names

# Join source0 and source1 on source0.name == source1.school
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, left_on="name", right_on="school", how="inner")

# Rename columns to target schema names
joined = joined.rename(columns={
    "name": "School Name",
    "grade": "Student Grade",
    "School ID": "School ID",
    "size": "School Size",
    "budget": "School Budget",
    "Student ID": "Student ID",
    "reading_score": "Student Reading Score",
    "math_score": "math_score"  # temporary name for aggregation
})

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns that appear unique and non-redundant in target:
# According to target schema and hints:
# Group by: School Name (string), Student Grade (string), School ID (int), School Size (int), School Budget (int)
group_cols = ["School Name", "Student Grade", "School ID", "School Size", "School Budget"]

# Aggregate:
# - Student ID: mean (float in target)
# - Student Reading Score: mean (float in target)
# - Average Student Math Score: mean of math_score (float in target)
agg_dict = {
    "Student ID": "mean",
    "Student Reading Score": "mean",
    "math_score": "mean"
}

grouped = joined.groupby(group_cols).agg(agg_dict).reset_index()

# Rename aggregated math_score to 'Average Student Math Score'
grouped = grouped.rename(columns={"math_score": "Average Student Math Score"})

# Ensure column order matches target schema exactly
final_cols = [
    "School Name",
    "Student Grade",
    "School ID",
    "School Size",
    "School Budget",
    "Student ID",
    "Student Reading Score",
    "Average Student Math Score"
]

final_df = grouped[final_cols]

# Write output
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
